title: content.replace reaches a WordPress theme's render-time words through content.renderedWords, only where the page showed them, and only from Tracy's agent
steps: S1: With TEST_DATABASE_URL set, run node --test on packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/replace-wordpress-rendered-words.test.mjs, packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/relay-origin.test.mjs, apps/tracy-web/test/component.test.mjs.

S2: Read the test names it reports for: a theme-printed phone replaced with its tel: link in one apply; a tel: link a record holds left out of the rules; a following tel: link printed away from the words (elsewhere in main, or in another element) left as it is, and one right beside the words followed; href:true refused under where:"main" for a header link and written for a link in main; content.renderedWords sent straight to the Apply door by a browser cookie or a seat key refused ACTION_AGENT_ONLY before the site, while the agent host's actor is taken and that apply is then listed and undone by apply.list and apply.revert; the engine's call relayed under the typing person's actor; the door's refusal of a cookie relay answered with the words kept; an inspect match outside the page-read location refused; and an older plugin answered with render-time wording.
expect: S1: exit 0 with no failed or skipped test.
S2: each of the behaviours has a passing test.
evidence: Before this change Diner WP's contact block, a PHP pattern printed through the_content, kept the template's sample address and phone because content.replace found no store holding them
fence: Host-side planning with recorded plugin answers; the plugin's own behaviour is covered by the claude-cowork WordPress suite and a real Diner WP stand
